name: Code as Action (CodeAct)
question: Should the agent write code instead of calling tools one at a time?
summary: The agent’s action is a short program rather than a single tool call. Tools are exposed as functions, and the model writes code with loops, variables and conditions that calls them, runs it in a sandbox and reads the output. Multi-step data work takes far fewer turns and tokens, but running model-written code needs isolation: no network by default, only allow-listed tools and libraries, time and memory limits, and review of anything that writes.
useCases: Bulk or repetitive work: reconciling hundreds of records, transforming files
Calculations and data analysis the model should not do in its head
Chaining several tools where each output feeds the next

items.detail: the model calls typed Python functions, not JSON one at a time
a container or micro-VM with no network by default
only named tools and imports are available
CPU time, memory, output size and number of turns
stdout, errors and return values go back to the model
writes and payments still pass policy checks or a person

steps: Expose tools as typed functions with docstrings
Run the model’s code in a sandbox with no network, allow-listed tools and limits
Return output and errors so the model can fix and retry
Keep writes behind the same policy checks as normal tool calls
pitfalls: Running generated code on the host with network access
Letting code import anything, including shell and HTTP libraries
Assuming code actions are safe because the model wrote them
remember: Let it write code, but run the code in a box.
caption: Illustrative: Bazaarkart, a fictional marketplace, reconciles 200 orders across three tools.

code.text: from smolagents import CodeAgent, tool, InferenceClientModel
"""Payment status for an order. Args: order_id: the order id."""
"""Delivery status for an air waybill. Args: awb: the waybill number."""
executor_type="e2b",                   # remote sandbox, not the host
result = agent.run("Reconcile yesterday's orders: flag any where payment "
"and courier status disagree. Do not refund anything.")
# The model writes and runs code such as:

steps.title: Expose tools as typed functions
steps.text: Each tool is a Python function with a docstring and types. The model can call them inside its own code, in loops and conditions.

steps.title: Run the code in a sandbox
steps.text: The code runs in a remote sandbox, not on your server. By default it has no network and no access to your files or secrets.

steps.title: Allow-list what code may import
steps.text: Only named imports are permitted. A program that tries to import requests or subprocess fails before it runs.

steps.title: Cap steps and time
steps.text: At most 8 turns, with limits on CPU time and output. A runaway loop stops instead of burning tokens.

steps.title: Read output, fix, retry
steps.text: Printed results and errors go back to the model, which can correct its code in the next turn. Here the whole reconciliation takes 6 turns.

steps.title: Keep writes behind checks
steps.text: flag_order only marks orders for a person. Refunds and other writes still pass the same policy checks as any tool call.

cons: More attack surface if the sandbox leaks

practice.scenario: Bazaarkart, a fictional marketplace, reconciles yesterday's orders every morning. Instead of 600 separate tool calls, the agent writes a short Python loop that calls the orders, payment and courier tools as functions and flags mismatches. The code runs in a remote sandbox with no network, only the listed tools and one allowed import, and at most 8 turns. Flagged orders go to a person; the agent cannot refund.

industries.use: Reconciling orders, payments and deliveries in bulk
Answering data questions by writing and running pandas code

practice.analogy: Giving an accountant a spreadsheet formula instead of reading every row aloud, but on a locked office computer.

practice.note: The API clients are stubs. Executor options and model classes change between smolagents versions; check the documentation.

samples.code:
from smolagents import CodeAgent, InferenceClientModel, tool

@tool
def payment(order_id: str) -> str:
    """Return the payment status for an order.

    Args:
        order_id: The marketplace order id.
    """
    return payments_api.status(order_id)

@tool
def courier(awb: str) -> str:
    """Return the delivery status for a shipment.

    Args:
        awb: The air waybill number.
    """
    return courier_api.status(awb)

agent = CodeAgent(
    tools=[payment, courier],
    model=InferenceClientModel(),
    additional_authorized_imports=["datetime"],
    executor_type="e2b",
    max_steps=8,
)
print(agent.run("For these orders, list ids whose payment and courier status "
                "disagree: " + str(yesterdays_orders())))

numericDrill.question: A task takes 600 turns of single tool calls, each sending about 6,000 tokens. With code actions it takes 6 turns of 10,000 tokens. How many times fewer tokens does code use?

interview.question: When would you let an agent write and run code?
interview.answer: For bulk, repetitive or numeric work where a loop replaces hundreds of tool calls, and where you can run the code in an isolated sandbox with no network, allow-listed tools and imports, and limits. Keep writes behind the same policy checks.

interview.question: What can go wrong with code actions?
interview.answer: Model-written code can be steered by injected text into exfiltrating data or making unwanted writes. Run it in a sandbox, never on the host, and treat its tool calls like any other.

mistakes.mistake: Running generated code on the app server
mistakes.fix: Use an isolated sandbox with no network
